newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Q1 trade deficit falls sharply.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Q1 trade deficit falls sharply.

text.p: BOGOTA, June 6 Reuter - Colombia's trade deficit fell 19.8 percent in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the same period a year ago, according to the National Statistics Department DANE.
It said the deficit stood at $519.1 million FOB in the first quarter, against $647 million in the same three-month period last year.

Exports rose 1.5 percent, from $2.3 billion to $2.4 billion, while imports dropped 3.2 percent, from $3.24 billion CIF in the first quarter of 1996 to $3.14 billion in the first quarter of 1997, DANE said.

It said revenues from traditional exports such as crude oil, coffee and nickel rose 14.9 percent in the first quarter of 1997 versus the same period a year ago. Coffee revenues alone rose by a hefty 24.6 percent to $430.5 million against $345.5 in January- March 1996.

Based on figures from the National Coffee Growers' Federation, the Statistics Department said Colombia exported 2.65 million 60-kg bags of coffee in the first quarter, up from 2.36 million bags in the same period last year.
Oil export revenues totaled $671.8 million, meanwhile, up from $587.1 million in the first quarter of 1996.

Leading economic analysts and government officials predict that a surge in oil and coffee export revenues will allow Colombia's economy to grow by as much as three percent this year despite negative growth of 1.22 percent in the first quarter.
Income from traditional exports totaled $1.32 billion FOB in the first quarter against $1.15 billion in the same period a year ago, DANE said.
